name: Small 4-regular graph of girth 10 (cage problem n(4,10))
description: Construct a 4-regular graph with no cycle shorter than 10 on as few vertices as possible. The smallest known such graph has 320 vertices (Exoo, Goedgebeur, Jooken, Stubbe and Van den Eede, 2026) and the best lower bound is 243.

sources.locator: Exoo, Goedgebeur, Jooken, Stubbe and Van den Eede, Electron. J. Combin. 33(3) (2026) P3.48 (arXiv:2511.07247), Table 2: n(4,10) >= 243, previous upper bound 384, new upper bound 320; Figure 4 lists the base graph and the group SmallGroup(40,10) = C5 x D4 of the lift.
Record graph n320_k4_g10.g6 in graph6 format (GPL-3.0).
Exoo and Jajcay, Dynamic cage survey (Electron. J. Combin. DS16): definitions, Moore bound and record tables.

requirements.datasets: None; the instance is defined by the parameters and no file is read at evaluation time.

evaluation.benchmark: Small 4-regular graph of girth 10 (cage problem n(4,10))
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: construct(k, g) -> (n, edges): the number of vertices n and a list of edges (i, j) on vertices 0..n-1; the evaluator passes this task's degree k and girth g. The graph must be simple (no loops or repeated edges), every vertex must have degree exactly k, and no cycle may be shorter than g (certified exactly with non-backtracking walks from every vertex). n must lie between the Moore bound and max_vertices. Score: n, minimized; it is an upper bound on the cage order n(k, g).

limitations: The evaluator accepts at most 50,000 vertices; the explicit Lazebnik-Ustimenko-Woldar seed has 512 vertices.
Connectivity is not required; a disconnected graph only has more vertices than its components.

The record construction is public, so a candidate can reproduce the record by embedding it; the score measures the returned object, not the search that produced it, and only a strictly smaller score than the best known value is a new result.
Candidate Python runs inside the evaluator process as trusted research code; the evaluator recomputes every property of the returned object exactly and trusts nothing the candidate reports.

state_of_the_art.statement: The smallest known 4-regular graph of girth 10 has 320 vertices (Exoo, Goedgebeur, Jooken, Stubbe and Van den Eede, 2026), found by the authors' computer search over graph lifts with voltage group SmallGroup(40,10) = C5 x D4; it improved 384 (the Exoo-Jajcay dynamic cage survey). The best lower bound is 243, so n(4,10) is open.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Determine the cage order n(4,10), the least number of vertices of a 4-regular graph of girth 10.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: The cage problem (Tutte 1947; Erdos and Sachs 1963) is a fundamental extremal problem of graph theory: it asks how small a regular graph with no short cycles can be. Graphs of high girth underlie LDPC codes and network constructions, the Moore bound is attained only in rare cases, and exact cage orders are known only for a few small parameters, so smaller graphs improve long-standing records.

papers.title: New small regular graphs of given girth: the cage problem and beyond

papers.task_relation: The task asks for a 4-regular graph of girth 10 on fewer than 320 vertices, the record of this paper (lower bound 243).
